run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The recommendation path is broken: the frontend's HTTP GET /recommendations returns 500 because its gRPC call /recommendation.Recommendation/GetRecommendations fails in 13-34 microseconds with no server span ever recorded, while every other frontend flow (/hotels, /search, /rate, /profile, /reservation, /user) succeeds and the recommendation pod itself is Running/Ready with 0 restarts and clean startup logs. The only network policy in the cluster, NetworkPolicy hotel-reservation/deny-all-recommendation (policyTypes Ingress and Egress with no ingress/egress rules, podSelector io.kompose.service=recommendation, created 2026-11-21T11:26:10Z), removes all allowed traffic for the recommendation pod (which that selector matches), which is the object blocking the frontend->recommendation gRPC path. The whole namespace was (re)created at 11:25:55-11:26:12 with unchanged image digests, and the frontend pod template changed at 11:26:10; neither is shown to be the fault itself, and no change history is available to say who created the policy.

claims.text: Frontend HTTP GET /recommendations fails: 10 sampled error spans at 11:26:23.6-11:26:23.9Z carry http.status_code=500 and otel.status_code=ERROR, each paired with a child client span /recommendation.Recommendation/GetRecommendations with otel.status_code=ERROR lasting only 13-34 microseconds.

In the full trace 69e201dbde1721e7 the failing frontend HTTP span (73 us) and its child /recommendation.Recommendation/GetRecommendations span (34 us) are the only two spans; no server-side span from the recommendation service exists in that trace.
Jaeger's service list contains frontend, geo, profile, rate, reservation, search and user but not recommendation, so no span of the recommendation service was seen since Jaeger started (11:25:57Z).

NetworkPolicy hotel-reservation/deny-all-recommendation has podSelector io.kompose.service=recommendation, policyTypes [Ingress,Egress] and no ingress or egress rules (deny-all), and was created at 2026-11-21T11:26:10Z.
deny-all-recommendation is the only NetworkPolicy anywhere in the cluster (cluster-wide query returned exactly this one object in namespace hotel-reservation).
The policy's selector matches the running recommendation pod: a server-side label query io.kompose.service=recommendation returned exactly one pod, recommendation-86cf75495d-6hprg.

The recommendation pod recommendation-86cf75495d-6hprg (pod IP 10.244.125.50, matching the address it registered with) is Running and Ready with restartCount 0 and no previous terminated container, and the recommendation Deployment reports 1/1 ready replicas.

Recommendation application logs show a clean start: DB session successful at 11:26:06Z, 'Starting server...', and 'Successfully registered in consul' for srv-recommendation at address 10.244.125.50:8085 at 11:26:06.430Z; no error-level lines are present in the 20 lines returned.
The recommendation Deployment exposes containerPort 8085 and defines neither a readinessProbe nor a livenessProbe, so an unreachable-but-running pod still reports Ready.

Other frontend paths are healthy at the same time: three HTTP GET /hotels spans return http.status_code=200 (4.5-5.6 ms) with successful child calls /search.Search/Nearby, /geo.Geo/Nearby, /rate.Rate/GetRates, /profile.Profile/GetProfiles and /reservation.Reservation/CheckAvailability, none with error status.

The rate service's own metrics at 2026-11-21T11:26:24Z show rate_backend_qps_limit=500, rate_requests_rejected_total=0, rate_requests_expired_total=0 and rate_queue_depth=0, with 107 requests received; search recorded 384 rate attempts.

The whole hotel-reservation namespace was (re)created in a rollout at 11:25:55-11:26:12Z (all 19 deployments scaled up replica sets; mongodb-geo-78487c9767 and mongodb-rate-6747cb74bf scaled to 0, frontend-68745cb99c scaled down at 11:26:12) and every hotel-reservation workload uses the same image digest sha256:1c685e1c..., so this was not an image change.

The frontend Deployment only reached generation 2 with a second ReplicaSet frontend-58f94bb887 created at 2026-11-21T11:26:10Z (old frontend-68745cb99c scaled to 0 at 11:26:12Z), and the new pod's env is only JAEGER_SAMPLE_RATIO=1 — simultaneous with the network policy creation, not shown to be the fault by itself.
Every hotel-reservation Service has endpoints, including recommendation (10.244.125.50, port 8085), so this is not a selector/endpoints misconfiguration.

The deny-all-recommendation NetworkPolicy is the object that removes all allowed ingress/egress for the recommendation pods, and the frontend's calls to /recommendation.Recommendation/GetRecommendations are the only RPCs failing (in tens of microseconds, before any server span), which is the path that policy blocks; the policy was created 13 seconds before the first observed failures and after the recommendation pod had registered itself, so this policy is the fault applied to the recommendation workload.

Mechanism hypothesis: because the policy has no ingress rule, the frontend's gRPC connection to 10.244.125.50:8085 cannot be established, and the Consul health check from the agent to the recommendation pod is likewise blocked, so the grpc/lb/consul resolver can return no passing instance and the call fail-fasts in ~13-34 us without a network round trip. The fail-fast behaviour is observed; the Consul catalog/health state behind it was not directly readable.

Secondary consequence hypothesis: the policy's Egress deny also isolates the recommendation pod from mongodb-recommendation:27017 and from the Jaeger/otel collector, which would explain why it emits no spans after 11:26:10Z; the pod's own post-policy connection errors were not captured in its logs, which stop at 11:26:06Z.

The recommendation service process itself shows no failure: pod Running/Ready, 0 restarts, no previous terminated container, DB session and Consul registration logged as successful, and its Deployment is 1/1 ready — the failure is connectivity to it, not its own crash or DB startup error.

The frontend is not broadly broken: it serves /hotels with HTTP 200 and completes all of its downstream gRPC calls (search, geo, rate, profile, reservation) successfully, and its startup log shows gRPC clients for srv-search, srv-profile, srv-recommendation, srv-user and srv-reservation initialized successfully.

Rejected: the rate service's QPS-limit fault-injection knobs (RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT=500, RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY=256) causing rejections/expiry. The rate service reports 0 rejected, 0 expired, queue depth 0 and 107 requests received, /rate.Rate/GetRates spans in the successful /hotels traces carry no error status, and the failing operation does not call rate.

Rejected as this incident's cause: the MongoDB admin-privilege fault scripts stored in ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo and failure-admin-rate (revoke/drop admin user on geo-db / rate-db). They are dormant script text only, no Job exists in hotel-reservation to run them, and geo and rate calls in the sampled traces complete without error.

Rejected: recommendation pod crash/restart or scheduling failure as the cause. The pod has restartCount 0 and no last termination reason, and the only Warning scheduling events (FailedScheduling on mongodb-geo-78487c9767-rp482 and mongodb-rate-6747cb74bf-bnp2x at 11:25:59Z) belong to MongoDB pods that the Deployment controller replaced during the rollout, not to recommendation.

Remove (or fix) NetworkPolicy hotel-reservation/deny-all-recommendation — delete it or replace it with explicit allow rules for ingress from the frontend pods on 8085 and egress to mongodb-recommendation:27017 and consul:8500 — then re-test GET /recommendations end to end.
Add readiness/liveness probes to the recommendation Deployment (containerPort 8085) so that loss of reachability is visible as NotReady instead of a Ready pod that answers nothing.

Correlate the policy creation at 2026-11-21T11:26:10Z (and the frontend pod-template generation bump at the same second) with cluster change history or the deployment pipeline, since change history is not integrated in this Run.

gaps: change_history is not integrated in this Run, so who created NetworkPolicy deny-all-recommendation at 11:26:10Z and why, and what changed the frontend pod template at the same second, cannot be determined.

The Consul catalog/health state of srv-recommendation was not directly observable; whether the resolver returned zero passing instances because the deny-all policy blocks the Consul health check is inferred, not measured (the consul log line for a health-service query at 11:26:11Z does not show the response body).

Trace coverage is a ~0.3 second sample (11:26:23.64-11:26:23.95Z) and the app metrics have a single sample at 11:26:24Z; there is no pre-fault baseline, since the namespace's pods only started at 11:25:55-11:26:12Z, so no latency trend or error-rate comparison can be made.
Recommendation pod logs stop at 11:26:06.430Z (last startup line), so no post-policy application error from that pod was observed; whether it logged blocked DB/Consul connections is unknown.
Whether the recommendation pod can reach mongodb-recommendation after 11:26:10Z is unverified because of the Egress deny.

Whether the deny-all policy is actually enforced by the cluster CNI is inferred from the failure timing and fail-fast client spans rather than measured directly (no packet-drop or CNI logs available).

Several queries returned no data and are limits of this Run, not evidence of absence: a Jaeger search for service 'search' with error=true, for service 'recommendation', and for error=true on frontend HTTP GET /hotels, HTTP POST /reservation, HTTP POST /user, /search.Search/Nearby, service rate and service geo all matched nothing; a pod-level label/column query for recommendation-86cf75495d-6hprg with readiness conditions returned INVALID_PARAMS; a query for Jobs in hotel-reservation and for pods in namespace default returned no objects, so the absence of a fault-injection Job runner for the failure-admin-geo / failure-admin-rate ConfigMaps is only a no-data result, not proof it never ran; and a metric-name query for rpc_server_duration/http_server_request_duration series returned no data, so no gRPC/HTTP error or latency series for those names exists in this Run.
next_steps: Read the cluster's change history / API audit to identify the principal and reason for creating hotel-reservation/deny-all-recommendation at 2026-11-21T11:26:10Z.

Delete or correct the deny-all-recommendation policy (allow frontend->recommendation:8085 ingress and recommendation->mongodb-recommendation:27017 / consul:8500 egress) and re-run the /recommendations flow to confirm recovery.
Add probes to the recommendation Deployment and an alert on GET /recommendations 5xx so isolation of that pod is detected without relying on a single endpoint's error spans.

{"remove-admin-mongo.sh":"#!/bin/bash


ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

echo "Removing admin user..."

mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.dropUser('admin');"

echo "Admin user removed successfully"
","remove-mitigate-admin-geo-mongo.sh":"#!/bin/bash


ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"
READ_WRITE_ROLE="readWrite"
TARGET_DB="geo-db"

echo "Recreating admin user..."

# Connect to MongoDB and create the admin user
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ADMIN_USER', pwd: '$ADMIN_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

echo "Admin user recreated"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ADMIN_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

echo "Privileges restored successfully"
","revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh":"#!/bin/bash


ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"
# TARGET_DB="rate-db"
TARGET_DB="geo-db"

echo "Downgrading admin user privileges..."

# Connect to MongoDB and revoke roles
mongo admin -u $ADMIN_USER -p $ADMIN_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.revokeRolesFromUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: 'readWrite', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

echo "Privileges downgraded"
","revoke-mitigate-admin-geo-mongo.sh":"#!/bin/bash


ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"

# TARGET_DB="rate-db"
TARGET_DB="geo-db"
READ_WRITE_ROLE="readWrite"

echo "Restoring readWrite privilege to the $ADMIN_USER user for the $TARGET_DB database..."

# Grant readWrite role on the target database
mongo admin -u $ADMIN_USER -p $ADMIN_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

echo "Privilege restored successfully"
"}

{"k8s-geo-mongo.sh":"#!/bin/bash


ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"

ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

TARGET_DB="geo-db"
READ_WRITE_ROLE="readWrite"

echo "Waiting for MongoDB to start..."
until mongo --eval "print('waited for connection')" > /dev/null 2>&1; do
  sleep 1
done
echo "MongoDB started"

# Create the admin user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating admin user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ADMIN_USER', pwd: '$ADMIN_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ADMIN_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ADMIN_USER -p $ADMIN_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

# Create the root user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating root user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ROOT_USER', pwd: '$ROOT_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database to root
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ROOT_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ROOT_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"


echo "Initialization script completed"
"}
